newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso halts slide, speculation eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso halts slide, speculation eases.

text.p: The Mexican peso moderated its earlier slide against the dollar at the close of trade on Monday, due to brokers selling dollars they had previously bought in speculative dealing, traders said.
"There was no no real flow, they were just speculating," a trader said. "Many dealers bought dollars they did not need and sold them once they saw the peso did not slide further."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.45 and 0.5 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8680/7.8710 and 7.8710/7.8740 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso also weakened against the dollar due to several banks covering short dollar positions after exercising some dollar puts on Friday with the central bank.

"I feel they exercised puts on Friday, but had not bought dollars," another trader said. "For that reason, they opened the session short and the peso weakened as they bought dollars to cover those shorts."
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.3 centavos weaker at 7.8700/7.8740 per dollar.

Dealers said developments in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday would depend on forecast results for the primary auction of government securities to be held by the central bank after the close of trade.
"We only expect marginal cuts in primary rates," one trader said.
